title: I built a Trackmania-style racer where you’re a single wheel, in 3 weeks with Claude Opus 5.5: the trick was making the AI measure instead of guess
author: RepublicLatter4835
selftext:
**Rim Runner** is a Trackmania-style time-attack racer where you *are* a wheel: lean into corners, land clean, chase hundredths on online leaderboards. Godot 4 + Jolt, solo, started 27 September. Claude Code wrote almost all of the code (39k lines, 678 automated checks); I play, judge and decide whats fun. 

**What made it work: never let the AI guess about feel.**

* **My runs as data.** The game keeps my replays and the last seconds of every restart. When I say “I keep falling here”, Claude compares my best run with the falls, frame by frame.
* **Labs, not opinions.** “The jumps feel too short” became a tool that measures the real flight off every ramp in the game’s physics, then resizes every gap to my speed.
* **Every fix gets a test.** Today a bounce-wall jump turned into an accidental backflip: Claude found I press 0.1-0.3 s after the wall, restored the old behavior and added a test.
* **Bots timed to a human.** Levels come from a Python generator; moving obstacles are timed to my pace, not to bots that wait at every gate.

The synthwave soundtrack is made with Eleven Music, the tire impact sounds with ElevenLabs. What AI didn’t do: decide what’s fun.

Free, plays in the browser: [https://jbtieb.itch.io/rim-runner](https://jbtieb.itch.io/rim-runner)  
Dev updates on X: [https://x.com/JBTiebb](https://x.com/JBTiebb)

Happy to go deeper on the workflow, and tell me your time on the Skill Tower (Elite is 13.5 s).
